newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - Dlr/mark volatility up on Yeltsin illness.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Dlr/mark volatility up on Yeltsin illness.

text.p: Implied volatilities for short-dated dollar/mark options spiked higher on Wednesday as the mark continued to come under pressure amid speculation about the health of Boris Yeltsin.
The Kremlin confirmed that the Russian president has early signs of pneumonia and has been sent to hospital.
The news sent the mark, already weakened by rumours that Yeltsin suffered from a cold, to fresh lows.
"It spiked a bit on the news. The dollar went from the 70 level (1.5770 marks) up to new highs," said Oliver Jefferson, vice president at Societe Generale.

At 1300 CST/1900 GMT, implied volatility for one-month dollar/mark at-the-money options was 9.5/9.8 percent, dealers said. An hour earlier, before confirmation of Yeltsin's illness, volatilities had been trading 0.15 percentage point below that level, although still up on the day amid rumors he had a cold.
Late Tuesday, implied volatility for one-month dollar/mark was 8.9 percent, dealers said.
Implied volatility for one-month dollar/yen options was slightly lower as concerns about a yen slide eased, dealers said.
The one-month contract was trading at 8.5 percent, roughly 0.20 percentage point below Tuesday's U.S. levels.
"They know that every time it (the dollar) goes up some other (Japanese) official comes out and makes some statement that pushes it back down," said one over-the-counter dealer with a British bank.
Cable volatility continued to trade at lofty levels although below recent highs, he said, quoting one-month implied volatility at 10.0/10.2 percent.
"We really need to see a few good closes above $1.70 to get vols really excited again," he said.
Implied volatilities for one-month dollar/Canada also held lofty levels near five percent as the Canadian dollar continued to gain strength.
One-month dollar/Canada began 1997 trading at four percent, dealers said. Implied volatility for one-year at-the-money options began January at 4.25 percent, compared with 4.7 percent on Wednesday.
Talk of heavy over-the-counter options activity in dollar/Canada was contributing to the bid, the dealer said.

"Nothing very clear has come out of it -- just that dollar/Canada has had a big slide over the past few days and a lot of people are saying there have been some large options done," the British dealer said.
A dealer with a Canadian bank noted talk of a very large OTC one-year strangle in dollar/Canada. However, other dealers had heard the option was a 15-delta call.
